title: Delete every Python file and committed __pycache__, ignore them in .gitignore, and replace the app command's Python launcher with a Go one
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

Where the serving line is printed: practice in main, crossdomain in run. Chosen: run, so the readiness test can read it.
How the readiness test observes N: practice polls GET and ignores refusals; crossdomain dials TCP and reads on the first connect. Chosen: the dial, which mirrors look_web.

Whether scope.Helper forwards to the parent or does nothing.

attempts.head: 89da1ad3d8055a4b6021326ca0f34b25ba7649dc
attempts.summary: Both proposals agree on everything that touches the real code, and each piece was checked against the tree.

caused_by.reason: Trip 1 of 2 back to the risk spike: the design left 1 fork that only a measurement can settle. O-017: unsettled design fork: Does an hband started on a data folder whose previous hband was killed with TerminateProcess (WAL and -shm left behind) serve every seeded row and report file, so that the e004-look page shows 'continue this thread' and the branch page and /raw/e004-look answer 200? Its context: Neither proposal disputes it, and both rest on it: the practice proposal marks it must-verify, and the crossdomain proposal marks it must-verify and requires an exit-verified stop. Nobody has measured it. It is settled in about 6 s by TestPortOpensOnlyOnceTheThreadIsSeeded, or by line 7 through -overlay. If the answer is no, both placements of the restart fail, and only a product-side change (for example, the program listening late) or the rejected front proxy is left. That would change the component boundary. The synthesis marked this as forcing a re-synthesis: the losing answer moves a component boundary, a contract or the data model. How the fork decider would measure it: Send this back to the risk spike to measure the restart. Do not hand it to the build. The spike must run the cut-over by itself, without building the launcher. SETUP. Make a scratch clone of slice/SL-017 at HEAD. Set TAAD3_HOME to a new empty scratch folder. Add one throwaway test file through `go test -overlay`, for example internal/testutil/program/zz_cutover_test.go in package program_test. Write nothing to the repository. No browser is needed; this uses only HTTP over loopback. WHAT THE TEST DOES, all through the unchanged harness: 1. `bin := program.Build(t)`, and `data := t.TempDir()`, checked with `outside.MustBeOutside`. 2. Pick two free loopback ports, P and N, with P != N. 3. Run the staging step inside `t.Run("staging", ...)`, so its cleanups run when the subtest ends: `s := program.Start(st, bin, Options{Port: P, Env: {"HBAND_DATA_DIR": data}})`, then `program.DeepThread(st, s)`. When the subtest ends, launch's cleanup kills the child with Process.Kill, which is TerminateProcess on Windows, and waits for it. 4. Before the final start, record: (a) that the staging hband.exe is gone, from its PID or from P refusing connections; (b) the data folder's listing: the size of the .db, -wal and -shm files, and the files under reports/. The -wal must be non-empty and the -shm must exist. If they are not, the shape was not exercised and the run counts as not measured, not as a pass. 5. `final := program.Start(t, bin, Options{Port: N, Env: same})`. 6. Check on N: - GET /reports/e004-look answers 200, contains 'continue this thread' and a /reports/e004-look/comments/<id> link; - that branch link answers 200; - GET /raw/e004-look answers 200 with the same bytes as the report DeepThread published (98 bytes, per the spike); - GET / contains src="/raw/e004-look"; - /reports lists e004-look; - the public comment count reads 9 comments, which is the whole 9-level chain across the report page and the branch page. 7. Run it 5 times with -count=1, and record each run's timings and its file listing. HOW THE RESULT DECIDES: - YES, all 5 runs pass with the -wal and -shm left behind: the design stands as written. Keep the restart in the launcher over a shared HBAND_DATA_DIR, and add no exit-verified stop beyond launch's 5-s wait. The result is evidence for O-014 and O-016. TestPortOpensOnlyOnceTheThreadIsSeeded stays the build's regression check. - Fails only when step 4(a) shows the staging child still alive at the final open: put crossdomain's exit-verified stop in the launcher. Confirm the child is gone, or Fatalf after 10 s, before the final Start. The component boundary does not move. - Fails with the staging child confirmed dead: the killed writer's state does not carry over. That covers missing comments, a 404 or 500 on /raw, a final start that Fatalfs with a database error, or a count below 9. Seed-then-serve is then dead in both placements. The fork goes back to design and must be escalated, because what is left (the product listening late, or the rejected proxy) moves the boundary into C-001's product code. Nothing measured so far covers this. The spike's runs used a single Start, and its Python run removed the folder after the kill, so no hband has ever opened a data folder left by a killed writer. Both proposals assume the same answer, and the synthesis marked it as forcing re-synthesis: a 'no' kills both placements of the restart and moves the component boundary into the product. The critique cited SQLite's documentation that committed transactions survive an application crash, so 'yes' is likely. That documentation still says nothing about modernc's Windows VFS recovering a left-behind -shm, or about the report file under reports/. Leaving it to the build would make the builder settle it by writing code, for example an ad hoc wait, a checkpoint or a proxy, with no record that a choice was made. It would also put the first evidence at validate (O-014), the most expensive place to find a 'no'. The measurement takes about 6-10 s per run, needs no person, no browser and no edit to the repository, and its result picks one of three concrete designs. This is lap 1 of 2. The risk spike measures these first. Write the design again with what it measured: its experiments are under what reality already said about this slice.
